newsitem.title: INDIA: India striving to win share in world flower market.
newsitem.headline: India striving to win share in world flower market.

text.p: India's floriculture industry, still in its infancy, could win a substantial share of the $40 billion world flower market if it received adequate government support, experts said on Thursday.
Industry officials said India was expected to export flowers valued at 300 million rupees ($8.4 million) in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March), up from 250 million the previous year.
"If additional steps are taken to export flowers on scientific lines it would become a potential source of valuable foreign exchange and boost the economy," said Foja Singh, a horticulture expert.

Singh told Reuters India lacked sophisticated storage and transportation facilities, making it difficult to compete with major flower exporting countries like Holland, Britain, the United States, Japan and Thailand.
He said the world market for floriculture products was growing 15 percent annually. India's share of the world market was just 0.01 percent.
India annually produces some 20,500 tonnes of cut flowers. Nearly 29,000 hectares of land is under ornamental crops.
Indian exports include roses, gladioli, carnations, chrysanthemums, lillies and jasmine. Main markets include the Gulf, Germany, France, Britain, Netherlands and Singapore.
Singh said Indian floriculture needed greenhouse technology at low prices to improve quality over field-grown crops.
"If only some of the constraints are removed by the government, India could be a serious contender in the international flower market," said another expert.
An auction house for flowers is also planned in the northern state of Haryana.

Several floriculture firms have sprung up in the past two years following relaxations in the kind of agricultural commodities under India's five-year-old economic reform programme. ($ = 35.8 Indian Rupees)
